Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:10:1.english: Decreased in value - [Meaning,] he was spoiled.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:10:2.hebrew: שאין מחשבין לו - את השנים שעליו לעבוד, אלא במנה, כאילו נמכר במנה. ולקמיה יליף לה, מאי חזית דדריש להו לקולא? וידו של עובד כוכבים על התחתונה, כדאמרן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:10:2.english: That one does not assess him - [for] the years that he still has to work, except at a maneh, as if he had been sold for a maneh. And later [the Gemara] derives it: What did you see that you interpret these [verses] leniently? [Because] the hand of the gentile is on the lower side, as we said.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:13:1.hebrew: אמר אביי הריני כבן עזאי - כי הוה בדיחא דעתיה, הוי רגיל למימר הכי: הריני פתוח ומוכן להשיב לשואלי דבר תורה, כבן עזאי שהיה דר בטבריא, שהיה חריף ודרשן. ואמר (בכורות כח.): כל חכמי ישראל לפני כקליפת השום, חוץ מן הקרח הזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:13:1.english: Abaye said: Behold, I am like ben Azzai - When he was in a good mood, he was accustomed to say this: I am open and ready to answer those who ask me a matter of Torah, like ben Azzai, who lived in Tiberias, who was sharp and a expounder. And he said (Bekhorot 28a): All the Sages of Israel before me are like the peel of garlic, except for this bald one.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:13:2.hebrew: נדרשינהו לחומרא - להחמיר על העבד: השביח — יתן כפי שניו, הכסיף — ישיב לפי מה שנאמר "כסף מקנתו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:13:2.english: Let us expound them stringently - To be stringent upon the slave: if he improved in value, he gives according to "his years"; if he declined in value, he repays according to [what is stated], "the money of his purchase."

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:13:3.hebrew: נדרשינהו לחומרא - להחמיר על העבד: השביח — יתן כפי שניו, הכסיף — ישיב לפי כסף מקנתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:13:3.english: Let us expound them stringently - To be stringent with the slave: if he improved in value, he gives according to his years; if he declined in value, he repays according to the money of his purchase.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:14:1.hebrew: מ"ש דקתני לא הרגיש - דמשמע אם לא הרגיש, סופו לבא לכך. ובכולהו תנא שנה לא באת לידו עד שמוכר, דמשמע דפשיטא ליה לתנא דדרכו בכך, דלא תבא לידו שישוב בתשובה עד שיקבל עוד פורענות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:14:1.english: As for what [the Tanna] teaches, "he did not sense [it]" - This implies that if he did not sense it, he will eventually come to this. And in all [these cases] the Tanna [taught] "it did not come to his hand until he was sold," which implies that it is obvious to the Tanna that this is his way: that it will not come to his hand to repent until he receives further punishment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:16:1.hebrew: מדרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא - שלא בא לידי עבדות אלא שהיה חשוד על שמירת השביעית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:16:1.english: From [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina - For [the Hebrew slave] came to slavery only because he was suspected of [violating] the Sabbatical year.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:16:2.hebrew: אבקה של שביעית - איסור הקל שבה. העושה סחורה בפירותיה, דהוה ליה לאו הבא מכלל עשה, שנאמר "לאכלה" (ויקרא כה) ולא לסחורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:16:2.english: A hint of the Sabbatical Year - The lightest prohibition in it. One who trades in its produce, for it is a prohibition derived from a positive commandment, [as it is stated] "to eat" (Leviticus 25) and not for trade.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:17:1.hebrew: בשנת היובל הזאת - ובסמוך לו: וכי תמכרו, אם תמכרו ותקנו מה שאסרתי לכם בו, סופך למכור ממכריך וכל כלי ביתך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:17:1.english: In this Jubilee Year - and juxtaposed to it: "And if you sell" — if you buy and sell that which I prohibited to you in it, in the end you will sell your wares and all your household utensils.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:18:1.hebrew: לא הרגיש - לא שם לבו לפורענות הבא עליו, לחזור בו מעבירה שבידו. גבי "לא הרגיש" גרסינן "לסוף שמוכר את שדותיו", וגבי "לא באת לידו" בכולהו גרסי' בתוספתא "עד שמוכר". והכי משמע: לא תבא בידו הרהור תשובה עד שבא לכל אלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:18:1.english: He did not sense - He did not take to heart the calamity that came upon him, to repent of the transgression that is in his hand. Regarding "he did not sense," we read "ultimately he sells his fields," and regarding "it did not come to his hand," in all of them we read in the Tosefta "until he sells." And this is the meaning: a thought of repentance will not come into his hand until he comes to all of these:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:19:1.hebrew: מ"ש דקתני לא הרגיש - דמשמע: אם לא הרגיש, סופו לבא לכך. ובכולהו תנא קתני "לא באת לידו" עד שמוכר, דמשמע דפשיטא ליה לתנא דדרכו בכך, דלא תבא לידו שישוב בתשובה עד שיקבל עוד פורענות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:19:1.english: What is different that it teaches “he did not sense” - For it implies: if he did not sense [the sin], he will eventually come to this [further sin]. But in all of [the later cases] the Tanna [teaches] “it did not come to his hand” until he sells [himself], which implies that it is obvious to the Tanna that this is his way: that [the opportunity] will not come to his hand to repent until he receives further punishment:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:1:1.hebrew: לקרובים - אע"ג שאין כאן יעוד, שאין קדושין תופסין בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:1:1.english: To relatives - Even though there is no designation here, [since] betrothal does not take effect with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:20:1.hebrew: אע"ג דבתו בהאי ענינא לא כתיבא - אף על גב שאין אפשר לדרוש בה סמיכת פרשה. מכל מקום, הואיל ופרשת רבית סמוכה לפרשת ממכר בית, אנן סהדי שכבר מכר את בתו, אם יש לו בת קטנה, קודם שלוה ברבית, דניחא ליה וכו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:20:1.english: Even though "his daughter" is not written in this matter - [even though one cannot] derive from it [a teaching] from the juxtaposition of passages. Nevertheless, since the passage of interest is adjacent to the passage of the sale of a house, we are witnesses that he already sold his daughter, if he has a minor daughter, before he borrowed with interest, because it is preferable to him, etc.:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:21:1.hebrew: וכי ימוך אחיך - הכל בסדר סמיכת פרשיות הוא דורשו, וכולן זו קשה משלפניה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:21:1.english: And if your brother grows poor - [The baraita] expounds all of it according to the order of the juxtaposition of the passages, and each of them is harsher than the one before it:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:22:1.hebrew: שנאמר לגר - פרשה אחרת היא, הסמוכה לנמכר לך, והיא וכי תשיג יד גר ותושב עמך וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:22:1.english: As it is stated: “To a stranger [ger]” - This is a different passage, adjacent to [the passage of] one who is sold to you, [namely]: “And if the means of a stranger and settler with you suffice,” etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:3:1.hebrew: ורבי מאיר - דדריש להאי קרא "לאמה" שהוא בפוסק ע"מ שלא לייעד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:3:1.english: And Rabbi Meir - who derives this [verse], “as a maidservant,” [as referring] to one who stipulates, on condition that she not be designated [for marriage]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:3:2.hebrew: כרבנן - לעיל בשמעתין, דקתני: אין מוכרה לקרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:3:2.english: In accordance with the Rabbis - Earlier in this passage, where it teaches: He may not sell her to relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:1.hebrew: אין מוכרה לאביו - שאסורה לו משום בת בנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:1.english: He cannot sell her to his father - Because she is forbidden to him [the father] as his son's daughter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:2.hebrew: ולא לבנו - דהויא ליה אחותו, ואין קידושין תופסין בחייבי כריתות, כדלקמן (קידושין דף סו:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:2.english: Nor to his son - For she would be his [the son's] sister, and betrothal does not take effect with those liable to karet, as [stated] below (Kiddushin 66b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:3.hebrew: אין מוכרה לאביו - שאסורה לו משום בת בנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:3.english: He cannot sell her to his father - Because she is forbidden to him [i.e., to the father] as his son's daughter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:4.hebrew: ולא לבנו - דהויא ליה אחותו, ואין קידושין תופסין בחייבי כריתות, כדלקמן (קידושין דף סו:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:4:4.english: And not to his son - For she would be his [the son's] sister, and betrothal does not take effect with those liable to karet, as [stated] below (Kiddushin 66b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:5:1.hebrew: היכא דאיכא צד יעוד - כשמוכרה לאביו, ויש לו בן, לייעדה לבנו, דהויא ליה בת אחיו. אבל כשמוכרה לבנו, אין כאן צד יעוד, לא לו ולא לבנו, דהויא ליה אחות אביו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:5:1.english: Where there is a possibility of designation - When he sells her to his father, and he (the father) has a son, he can designate her for his son, for she would be his brother's daughter. But when he sells her to his own son, there is no possibility of designation here, neither for him nor for his son, for she would be his father's sister.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:6:1.english: With his body he shall leave - [The Gemara] explains this below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:6:2.english: Alone he shall leave - [The Gemara] explains this below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:7:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא - לא תצא בראשי אברים כעבד, שיוצא ואין נוטל כלום, אבל זו תצא ותטול דמי עינה. קמ"ל קרא יתירא, דאין דין יציאה בחסרון אברים כלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:7:1.english: I would have said - [that a Hebrew maidservant] does not go free through [the loss of] the principal limbs like a [Canaanite] slave, who goes free and receives nothing; but this one [would] go free and also receive the value of her eye. [Therefore] the superfluous verse teaches us that the law of going free does not apply at all in cases of loss of limbs.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:8:1.hebrew: יחידי נכנס - לרבי אליעזר נמי משמע ליה "בגפו" לשון "בגופו", ומפרש ליה לומר: שאם בא בגופו יחידי, יצא יחידי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:8:1.english: He enters alone - According to Rabbi Eliezer too, "bageifo" (by himself) implies the language of "begufo" (with his body alone), and he interprets it to mean that if he came with his body alone — by himself — he shall leave alone.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:8:2.hebrew: מוסר לו - הרב מוסר לו שפחה כנענית על כרחו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:8:2.english: Provides him - [The master provides him with a Canaanite maidservant] against his will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:9:1.hebrew: שאין מחשבין לו - כשבא לגרע ולפדות את עצמו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:9:1.english: That one does not assess him - When he comes to deduct from his service and redeem himself.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:9:2.hebrew: אלא מנה - כמה מגיע ממנה לכל שנה של שש שנים — שתות מנה, וכמה מגרע לכל שנה. ואם נותרה שנה, נותן לו שתות מנה. ולא אמרינן: הרי השביח, שנתייקרה הפעולה, או החליף כח ועומד על מאתים, תמנה מאתים לפעולת שש שנים ויתן לו שליש מנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:9:2.english: Only one hundred - How much of it falls to each year of the six years — a sixth of the hundred — and how much he deducts for each year. And if one year remains, he gives him [i.e., the master] a sixth of the hundred. And we do not say: Behold, he has increased in value, so that the labor has become more valuable, or he has changed strength and now stands at two hundred, so let us count two hundred for the labor of six years, and he gives him a third of a hundred.

Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:9:3.hebrew: מכסף מקנתו - משעת מקנתו ישיב גאולתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 20a:9:3.english: “Out of the money that he was bought for” - From the time of his purchase, he shall pay back his redemption.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:15:1.hebrew: כל הקונה עבד עברי כקונה אדון לעצמו - וקשה: מאי "אדון"? די לו להיות כאדונו! ויש לומר, כדאיתא בירושלמי: דפעמים אין לו אלא כר אחת; אם שוכב עליו בעצמו, אינו מקיים "כי טוב לו עמך"; ואם אינו שוכב עליו וגם אינו מוסרו לעבדו, זו מדת סדום. נמצא שע"כ צריך למסור לעבדו, והיינו "אדון לעצמו":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:15:1.english: Anyone who acquires a Hebrew slave is like one who acquires a master for himself - This is difficult: What is the meaning of "master"? It should suffice for him to be like his master! And one can say, as stated in the Yerushalmi: Sometimes he has only one pillow; if he lies on it himself, he does not fulfill "for it is good for him with you"; and if he does not lie on it, but also does not give it to his slave, this is the trait of Sodom. It turns out that he must necessarily give it to his slave, and this is [the meaning of] "a master for himself."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:16:1.hebrew: אבקה של שביעית - פירוש: איסור קל שבה. דעיקר איסור שביעית אינו אלא בעבודת קרקע, כגון חרישה וזריעה; אבל משא ומתן אינו אלא עשה בעלמא — לאכלה ולא לסחורה. ומסברא, שבא לו עונש זה על משא ומתן, מדה כנגד מדה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:16:1.english: A hint of the Sabbatical Year - Explanation: [it means] a minor prohibition within it. For the main prohibition of the Sabbatical Year is only in working the land, such as plowing and sowing; but commerce is merely a positive commandment — [that the produce is] for eating and not for trade. And by reasoning, this punishment comes upon him for commerce, measure for measure:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:20:1.hebrew: הא קמ"ל ליזבון איניש ברתיה - אף על גב שמפדין אותה בעל כרחו, מכל מקום רבית קשה יותר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:20:1.english: "This teaches us: a person should sell his daughter" - Even though she is redeemed [from her master] against his will, nevertheless interest is harsher:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:22:1.hebrew: לעקר זה עבודת כוכבים - שסופה ליעקר: ד"ז שייך לע"ב: עבד ד' ופשו ליה תרתי, ניתיב ליה תרתי כפי שניו. פירש בקונטרס: לא איירי קרא לא בהשביח ולא בהכסיף. וקשה, דא"כ אמאי שני קרא בלישניה? נכתוב אידי ואידי "מכסף מקנתו" או "כפי שניו"! ואומר ה"ר ברוך, דה"פ: אם עוד רבות בשנים — דעבד תרתי ופשו ליה ארבע, ליתיב ליה ארבע מכסף מקנתו, בין הכסיף ובין השביח, משום שהוא סמוך לזמן כניסה טפי מזמן יציאה. ואם מעט נשאר בשנים — דעבד ארבע ופש תרתי, ניתיב ליה כפי שניו שהוא שוה עתה, והוא סמוך לזמן יציאה, בין הכסיף ובין השביח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:22:1.english: "To an offshoot" – this is idolatry - for its end is to be uprooted. This [comment] belongs to the end of [the previous] page: If he served four [years] and two remain for him, they should give him [for] the two according to his years. Rashi explained: The verse does not speak either of a case where [the slave] increased in value or of one where he decreased in value. And this is difficult, for if so, why does the verse change its wording? Let it write in both cases "from the money of his purchase" or "according to his years"! And Rabbi Baruch says that this is its meaning: If many years remain — [that is,] he served two and four remain for him — they should give him [the refund] from "the money of his purchase," whether he decreased in value or increased in value, because he is nearer to the time of entry than to the time of exit. But if few years remain — [that is,] he served four and two remain — they should give him "according to his years," [meaning] what he is worth now, since he is close to the time of exit, whether he decreased in value or increased in value.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:22:2.hebrew: לעקר - זה עבודת כוכבים, שסופה ליעקר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:22:2.english: “To an offshoot [le'ekker]” - this is idolatry, for it is destined to be uprooted:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:6:1.hebrew: שאינו יוצא בראשי אברים כעבד - דס"ד דלא גרע מעבד כנעני, שאינו יוצא בשש ויובל ובגרעון כסף, ועובד את הבת, ואפילו הכי יוצא בראשי אברים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 20a:6:1.english: That he does not go free through [the loss of] limbs, like a slave - For one might have thought that he is no worse off than a Canaanite slave, who does not go free after six years, or at the Jubilee, or through payment of money [to redeem him], and who also serves the master's daughter, and nevertheless goes free through [the loss of] limbs:
